newsitem.title: UK: New Zealand seeks name of its own for kiwi fruit.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand seeks name of its own for kiwi fruit.

text.p: They're green, they're hairy and they're known the world over as kiwi fruit -- but a New Zealand trade group is rebranding the country's kiwis as Zespri to differentiate its fruit from those grown elsewhere.
The New Zealand Kiwi Fruit Marketing Board is acting to reclaim the country's lead in the kiwi market.
Backed up by a $60 million worldwide marketing campaign, Zespri-branded kiwis will be launched in the next six months, Andy Milligan, a director of branding consultants Interbrand, told Reuters.
Although kiwi fruit are also grown in South America and the U.S., it was New Zealand that first began to aggressively market kiwi fruit -- technically Chinese gooseberries -- in the 1960s.

"New Zealand began marketing Chinese gooseberries as kiwi fruit years ago, but unfortunately they didn't register the name. It has become a generic term and everyone growing them outside New Zealand calls them kiwi fruit too," Milligan said.
"Kiwi's grown in New Zealand are of a higher quality than those grown elsewhere in the world so the (kiwi board) wanted something to differentiate their fruit," said Milligan.
Interbrand spent six months developing the Zespri name, which is a combination of zest -- meaning fruit and energy, and espirit -- the French word for spirit.
"We used crossword freaks and word game addicts around the world to come up with names, and we also used a computer software programme to work on their best suggestions" said Milligan,
Interbrand worked with trademark and copyright lawyers to ensure the chosen name was not already in use.

In the next six months consumers in the Pacific Rim, Southeast Asia and Europe will find Zespri stickers on kiwis grown in New Zealand, while also being bombarded with advertising and promotional activities for the brand.
Milligan said he is confident the new name will be a success.
"It is possible to give fruit a brand name rather than just seeing it as a commodity. Israel brands oranges as Jaffa and South Africa uses the name Outspan for its oranges," he said.
